title: mqttpc processes
description: The processes this instance may run. A name that is not in here cannot be started over MQTT, so this file is the allowlist — keep it as small as the job needs.

propertyNames.description: process name; becomes an MQTT topic level, so no slashes, + or #

path.description: absolute path of the program to run

args.description: arguments, one per element (never a single string of them)

env.description: environment; replaces mqttpc's rather than adding to it

uid.description: run as this user id — only possible when mqttpc itself runs as root

gid.description: run as this group id — only possible when mqttpc itself runs as root

shell.description: run through a shell. Only needed for pipes and redirections; without it path and args are passed to execve untouched, which is safer

disableStdin.description: refuse set/<name>/pipe, so nothing from MQTT reaches this program's stdin

comment.description: free text, ignored — JSON has no comments

stdout.description: how stdout is published (default: stream). drop: not published. stream: each chunk as it arrives. buffer: collected and published as one message when the process exits. The _retain variants publish retained, which only makes sense for output you want to survive a restart

stderr.description: how stderr is published (default: stream). drop: not published. stream: each chunk as it arrives. buffer: collected and published as one message when the process exits. The _retain variants publish retained, which only makes sense for output you want to survive a restart

output.description: stdout and stderr combined, in the order they were flushed, on <name>/status/<proc>/output (default: drop — leaving it on would publish everything twice). drop: not published. stream: each chunk as it arrives. buffer: collected and published as one message when the process exits. The _retain variants publish retained, which only makes sense for output you want to survive a restart

bufferMax.description: bytes kept in buffer mode; older output is dropped and the message says how much

stdinFromSpawnPayload.description: the spawn payload is written to stdin, which is then closed — a one-shot command with its input in one message

enqueueSpawns.description: a spawn while it is already running waits its turn instead of being refused
